THE SHANGHAI TIMES, MONDAY, MARCH 1, 1937

Nanking Political Prisoners
Now Housed In New Home

Building Includes Many Modern Features, But Iron
Bars Prevent Escape; Elaborate Programme Of
Political Instruction A Salient Feature

NANKING:—Living in seclusion, about 200 political offenders, including 30 women, in the Metropolitan Reformatory in the suburbs of Nanking are being led through the educational channel to repent their former misdeeds and become useful and patriotic citizens.

Situated on a scenic hillside outside the Hoping-men (Gate) of the capital, and equipped with modern facilities, the new buildings of the Reformatory which were inaugurated on February 23, provide an ideal place for the conversion of the political offenders, being mostly ex-Communists.

The new Reformatory built mainly of brick and cement is of the most up-to-date style for this kind of structure. Near the main entrance is the administration building, housing an assembly hall, a reception room and office rooms. It is flanked on both sides by dormitories for the staff. Behind this building are the living quarters of the inmates. Here are airy living rooms, classrooms, bathrooms, toilet rooms, dining halls and a library. To better impress the inmates with political ideals and moral principles of the late Party leader Dr. Sun Yat-sen the quarters are given such names as min chu (nationalism) min chuan (democracy), min sheng

watch over their thought and better convert them the doyen system is adopted. Each instructor acts as a doyen to several inmates, and is responsible for their moral reform. He holds frequent conferences with individual inmates to analyze their thought and induce them on to the right path of thinking.

For classwork the men inmates are divided into three classes and the women inmates also into three classes in accordance with their background of thought and standard of learning. For those who are advanced in knowledge there is a research class, in which the inmates do research work in various fields under the guidance of their instructors.

Though confined in the Reformatory, the inmates are not without amusement Every week a movie is shown by the Central Movie Studio. Dramatic performances are also frequently given by the inmates themselves.

In order that the inmates may earn a independent living after leaving the Reformatory they are taught various productive arts. Men learn printing, horticulture or farming while women, sewing, embroidering, dyeing, or laundry.

Political criminals who are admitted into the Reformatory are confined for a period of six months. At the end of the period they are subject to examination by an examination board composed of the director and sectional chiefs of the Reformatory, a representative of the Central Kuomintang Headquarters, a judge from the Supreme Court and a prosecutor from the Chief Prosecutor's Office of the Supreme Court. Those who are found to have completely discarded their reactionary thought and become law-abiding and patriotic citizens will be released but those who are found to need further reform will be detained in the Reformatory for another six months, after which they will be subject to a re-examination. However, the total length of time of repeated detention is not to be over five years.

The suggestion of establishing a reformatory in the capital for the conversion of political offenders was advanced in 1929 to the Central Government by Mr. Liao Wei-fan. Owing to financial stringency, the idea was not carried out until January 1, 1936 when the Metropolitan Reformatory was inaugurated in its temporary premises in the city. The same year a piece of land, measuring 150 mow at Chihsiangtsun outside the Hoping Gate was purchased. Construction of the new buildings were started in April and completed toward the end of the year. The total outlay for the purchase of land and the construction of buildings were $240,000.

The Reformatory is now under the supervision of a director. The highest control organ is the Discipline and Administration Committee of which the director is concurrently chairman. Under the committee are five sections: discipline, investigation, work, health, police, and a police corps. The police are well-trained. They are required to attend classes in Party principles and other subjects of importance.

In addition to the Metropolitan Reformatory, eight others have been built respectively in the provincial capitals of Fukien, Chekiang, Anhwei, Kiangsu, Hupeh, Honan, Shansi, and Shantung, while three others have been projected in the provincial capitals of Szechwan, Kwangtung and Hopei. Connections are maintained between the Metropolitan Reformatory and the provincial reformatories already established.—Central News.

南京政治犯
现迁入新居

该建筑包含许多现代化设施，但铁栏防止逃脱；精心安排的政治教育计划是其显著特色

南京：—在南京郊区的首都感化院中，约200名政治犯（包括30名女性）过着与世隔绝的生活，正通过教育途径引导他们悔悟昔日的恶行，成为有用且爱国的公民。

该感化院新址位于首都和平门外的风景秀丽的山坡上，配备现代化设施，于2月23日正式启用，为政治犯（大多为前共产党人）的转化提供了理想场所。

新建的感化院主要由砖和水泥建成，是此类结构中最具现代风格的建筑。主入口附近是行政大楼，内设礼堂、接待室和办公室。大楼两侧是职员宿舍。此楼后面是囚犯的居住区。这里有通风良好的起居室、教室、浴室、厕所、餐厅和图书馆。为了更好地向囚犯灌输已故党领袖孙中山博士的政治理想和道德原则，各居住区被命名为“民族”（民族主义）、“民权”（民主）、“民生”

为了监视他们的思想并更好地转化他们，采用了导师制。每位导师负责几名囚犯，并负责他们的道德改造。导师经常与个别囚犯会谈，分析其思想，引导他们走上正确的思维道路。

在课堂学习方面，男囚犯根据其思想背景和文化程度分为三个班，女囚犯也分为三个班。对于知识水平较高者，设有研究班，囚犯在导师指导下在各个领域进行研究性工作。

虽然被拘禁在感化院内，但囚犯并非没有娱乐活动。中央电影制片厂每周放映一场电影。囚犯自己也经常进行戏剧表演。

为了使囚犯离开感化院后能够独立谋生，教授他们各种生产技艺。男性学习印刷、园艺或农耕，而女性学习缝纫、刺绣、染色或洗衣。

被收入感化院的政治罪犯监禁期为六个月。期满后，由感化院院长及各科室主任、国民党中央总部代表、最高法院法官及最高法院首席检察官办公室检察官组成的审查委员会对其进行审查。那些被发现已完全抛弃反动思想并成为守法爱国公民的人将被释放，而那些被认为需要进一步改造的人将在感化院再拘留六个月，之后将接受重新审查。然而，反复拘留的总时间不得超过五年。

1929年，廖维藩先生向中央政府提出了在首都建立感化院以转化政治犯的建议。由于财政紧张，该想法直到1936年1月1日才得以实施，当时首都感化院在市内的临时所址启用。同年，在和平门外的吉祥村购买了一块面积为150亩的土地。新建筑的建设于4月开始，并于年底完工。购地和建房的总支出为24万美元。

目前，感化院由一名院长监督。最高管理机构是纪律与管理委员会，院长兼任主席。委员会下设五个科：纪律科、调查科、作业科、卫生科、警务科，以及一支警察队伍。警察训练有素。他们被要求参加关于党义和其他重要科目的课程。

除首都感化院外，还在福建、浙江、安徽、江苏、湖北、河南、山西和山东的省会分别建立了八所感化院，另外计划在四川、广东和河北的省会建立三所。首都感化院与已建立的各省感化院保持联系。—中央通讯社。

MAYOR WU TE CHEN TO ENTERTAIN BRITISH AMBASSADOR

Mayor Wu Te Chen will give a dinner in honour of

THE ADMONITION OF POLITICAL OFFENDERS

With a view to correcting the thoughts of the
political offenders detained in the various district gaols
and in order to teach them the Three Principles of the
People, the local Tangpu recently inaugurated a Shanghai
Political Offenders Admonition Committee to interview
prisoners.
The admonition of the first batch of 103 political

September 30. Prisoners given a mark of excellent

Committee has decided to begin the admonition of the second
batch of political offenders on November 1.

October 1, 1936.

The "Holmes", a mosquito newspaper, publishes the following articles:-

"NIGHT BEFORE LAST"

About 11 o'clock last night, all was quiet in our alleyway. The people were fast asleep. Suddenly, there was great commotion, and everybody woke up trembling in the dark, chilly autumn night. Nobody knew what the trouble was.
Sounds of footsteps, heavy knocking at doors, the crying of babies, cursing and abusing in a strange tongue, assaulting of people, the shrieks of women, and the moving of furniture were clearly heard next door. All this made one's hair stand.
Another moment, somebody knocked at the door of my house. A maid-servant opened the door, and several men rushed in like robbers. Some went upstairs, others entered the kitchen and many more stood in the guest room. They all wore steel helmets with rifles in their hands. They assaulted every person whom they came across and damaged all the fine articles they saw. Cabinets and trunks were ransacked. My children cried for their mother; she stood behind me trembling. A shining bayonet was pointed at her back, a loud voice roared abuse telling her not to move.
Finally they searched my book case; many books were destroyed. Photographs hanging on the walls were torn up to see whether there was anything concealed in them. They found nothing. Before they left, my maid-servant was heavily kicked and I was rewarded with a blow while a vase in the guestroom was smashed to pieces.
Later, persons began to discuss when a second "January 28 Incident" would break out.

Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers (Sept. 30) :-

ADMONITION OF POLITICAL OFFENDERS

With a view to improving the thoughts of political offenders confined in prisons in Shanghai, the local Tangpu has organized a Political Offenders Admonition Committee with Pan Kung Chan (潘公展), Dong Yin Bei (童行白), Chiang Hwei Su (姜懷素), Loh Ching Sze (陸京士) and 23 others as members. Since the commencement of its work on July 1, 1936, about 103 political offenders; 97 in the 2nd Gaol, 4 in the 2nd Special District Gaol and 2 in the 1st Special District Gaol, have received admonition. As the period for the admonition of offenders expired on September 30, the Committee has decided to complete its admonition work. Reports of the various instructors on the standard of knowledge and the character of the political offenders have been forwarded to various prison authorities. Those who have a good record and have definitely repented will be granted a reduction of their sentence.
It is learned that investigations are being made into the number of such offenders confined in the various prisons so as to carry out the admonition work for the second period.

小报《Holmes》刊登以下文章：

“前夜”

昨晚11点左右，我们弄堂里一片寂静。人们都已熟睡。突然，一阵大骚动，每个人都在黑暗、寒冷的秋夜中颤抖着醒来。没人知道出了什么事。
隔壁清晰地听到脚步声、沉重的敲门声、婴儿的哭声、用陌生语言咒骂辱骂的声音、殴打人的声音、女人的尖叫声以及搬动家具的声音。这一切让人毛骨悚然。
过了一会儿，有人敲我家的门。一名女仆开了门，几个人像强盗一样冲了进来。一些人上楼，其他人进入厨房，还有许多人站在客厅里。他们都戴着钢盔，手里拿着步枪。他们袭击遇到的每一个人，并损坏了他们看到的所有精美物品。橱柜和衣箱被翻得乱七八糟。我的孩子们哭着找妈妈；她站在我身后发抖。一把闪亮的刺刀指着她的后背，一个大声的声音咆哮着辱骂，叫她不要动。
最后，他们搜查了我的书柜；许多书籍被毁坏。墙上挂着的照片被撕开，以查看里面是否藏有东西。他们什么也没找到。在他们离开之前，我的女仆被重重踢了一脚，我也挨了一拳，同时客厅里的一个花瓶被砸得粉碎。
后来，人们开始讨论第二次“一·二八事变”何时会爆发。

September 4, 1936.

Shun Pao and other local newspapers :-

MEASURES FOR THE SUPERVISION OF SURRENDERED COMMUNISTS

The local Committee to Examine Cases of Surrendered Communists was formed in autumn last year by the Tangpu, political and military organizations. Since its inauguration, the Committee has dealt with several hundred cases of surrendered Communists.

The Committee will hold a meeting next week to examine the cases of Communists who have applied for surrender. All youths who have taken the wrong path by mistake should call at the office of the Committee at Feng Ling Jao, Nantao, to apply for surrender. Certificates of surrender will be issued if their applications are approved by the Committee.

The Committee has drawn up the following measures for the supervision of surrendered Communists :-
1) These measures are drawn up for the purpose of supervising the movements of surrendered Communists so as to guard them against a relapse.
2) A Communist whose surrender has been approved by the Committee to Examine Cases of Surrendered Communists or whose surrender has been approved by an organization in another part of the country and who has removed to this city to reside is subject to supervision in accordance with these measures.
3) At the beginning of each month, a surrendered Communist should submit a report on his movements during the past month.
4) A surrendered Communist who intends to leave this city for proper cause must first secure the approval of this Committee which will request the organ of the district to which he intends to go to watch his movements on behalf of the Committee.
5) The guarantor of a surrendered Communist should, every two months, submit a report on the movements of the surrendered Communist for the past two months.
6) When the Committee thinks that a surrendered Communist will not have a relapse after these two kinds of reports have been received for over one year, either or both of these reports may no longer be required of him.
7) When a guarantor of a surrendered Communist finds out that the person whom he has guaranteed is about to repeat his crime, he should at once report the matter to the Committee or to some other proper organ to take action.
8) The Committee may at any time summon a surrendered Communist to the Committee for interrogation.
9) The Committee may notify a proper organ to arrest a surrendered Communist who had failed to submit a report on two successive occasions or who had failed to appear on two occasions when summoned by the Committee or who is about to repeat his crime.
10) Reformed Communists released from reformatories in the provinces in the country, who remove to this city, will be supervised according to these measures.

《申报》及其他本地报纸：-

监管投诚共产党人之措施

去年秋季，由当地党部及军政机关组建了“审查投诚共产党人案件委员会”。自该委员会成立以来，已处理了数百起投诚共产党人案件。

该委员会将于下周召开会议，审查申请投诚的共产党人案件。所有误入歧途的青年应前往南市凤林桥（Feng Ling Jao）的委员会办公室申请投诚。若申请获委员会批准，将颁发投诚证书。

委员会制定了以下监管投诚共产党人的措施：-
1) 制定这些措施的目的是为了监管投诚共产党人的行动，以防其重蹈覆辙。
2) 凡经“审查投诚共产党人案件委员会”批准投诚，或经国内其他地区组织批准投诚并迁居本市的共产党人，均须依照这些措施接受监管。
3) 每月初，投诚共产党人应提交一份关于其上月行动的報告。
4) 因正当理由拟离开本市的投诚共产党人，必须首先获得本委员会的批准；本委员会将请求其拟前往地区的机关代表本委员会监视其行动。
5) 投诚共产党人的担保人应每两个月提交一份关于该投诚共产党人过去两个月行动的报告。
6) 当委员会认为在收到上述两种报告超过一年后，某投诚共产党人不会重犯时，可不再要求其提交其中一种或两种报告。
7) 当投诚共产党人的担保人发现其所担保之人即将再次犯罪时，应立即向委员会或其他适当机关报告，以便采取行动。
8) 委员会可随时传唤投诚共产党人到委员会接受讯问。
9) 对于连续两次未提交报告、或连续两次未按委员会传唤到庭、或即将再次犯罪的投诚共产党人，委员会可通知适当机关予以逮捕。
10) 从各省感化院释放并迁居本市的改过自新的共产党人，将依照这些措施接受监管。

Organization at Shanghai of the "Committee for

Chinese Communist Party. Communist Suppression in China

In November 1935 the Nanking government Ministry of
Justice preconized the creation in towns or districts where no
penitentiaries exist for political prisoners committees, whose
task would be the re-educating of political prisoners. In
conformity with an order from the said Ministry, issued on
December 5, 1935, to the prison administration, this task would
devolve upon local Tangpus.

The "Committee for re-educating political prisoners at
Shanghai (上海政治犯教誨委員會)" was organized by the local Tangpu in
the beginning of May 1936. It is comprised of 25 members, whose
names are given in attached Appendix 1.

On May 8 the committee held its first meeting on the
premises of the local Tangpu. Mr TUNG YING PAI (童行白), member of
the executive committee of the said Tangpu, who presided,
explained the object of the Committee and gave an account of the
situation of political prisoners incarcerated in different prisons
in Shanghai. He gave the first results of work done by members of
the local Tangpu who visited the prisons in order to re-educate
political prisoners.

At the end of the meeting CHIANG HWEI SHOU (姜懷素), LOU
CHING CHIH (陸京士) and YING WAN (邢碗), members of the executive
committee of the local Tangpu, were elected permanent members of
the committee. Rules governing the committee in question are given
in Appendix 2. It has been established that 243 political prisoners

Rules governing the Committee for Re-education of Political
Prisoners in Shanghai.

1. The Committee to be organized by the Executive Committee of the
local Tangpu, in conformity with instructions given by the
Ministry of Justice.

Committee is
2. The created with the object of applying the special
penitentiary system to political prisoners incarcerated in
different prisons.

3. The Committee shall be comprised of 25 members of the Local
Tangpu and citizens of the district. Three permanent members
and a secretary will be designated by the executive committee
of the local Tangpu. They will concern themselves with the
current business of the committee for re-educating political
criminals.

4. All members of the Committee undertake to give lectures on
moral perfection to political criminals and this duty will be
undertaken in turn. The subjects of the lectures to be given
will be decided in advance by the Committee which will draw up
a catalogue for members so that these may deliver their lectures
at the appropriate time.

upon to give a penitence lecture.

right to make appeal to the employees of the local Tangpu. These
employees will not be paid.

will be granted locomotion expenses when travelling to give
penitence lectures.

ANNEXE II.

Règlements, gouvernant le comité chargé de la rééducation des
prisonniers politiques de Shanghai.

1. Le Comité doit être organisé par le comité exécutif du Tangpu
local, conformément aux instructions données par le Ministère de la
Justice.

2. Le Comité est créé dans le but d'appliquer le système péni-
tentiaire spécial, aux criminels politiques incarcérés dans les dif-
férentes prisons.

3. Le comité sera composé de 25 membres qui seront choisis par-
mi les membres du Tangpu Local et les citoyens du district. Trois
membres permanents et un secrétaire seront désignés par le comité
exécutif du Tangpu Local. Ils s'occuperont des affaires courantes
du comité pour la rééducation des criminels politiques.

4. Tous les membres du Comité s'engagent à donner des cours de
perfectionnement moral aux criminels politiques et leur service s'ef-
fectuera à tour de rôle. Les thèmes des cours à donner seront fixés
d'avance par le Comité qui établira un catalogue qui sera remis aux
membres pour qu'ils puissent faire leurs cours au fur et à
mesure.

5. Aucun membre du comité ne devra s'absenter lorsqu'il sera
appelé à donner les cours de pénitence.

6. En cas de nécessité, le Comité se réservera le droit de faire
appel aux employés du Tangpu Local. Ces employés ne seront pas payés.

7. Les membres du comité ne seront pas salariés. Il leur sera
accordé des frais de déplacements lorsqu'ils se dérangeront pour al-
ler donner des cours de pénitence.

MEASURES GOVERNING CONTROL OF SURRENDERED COMMUNISTS

With a view to preventing repentant communists from conducting further activities, the Censorship Committee to Deal With Surrenders of Communists in Shanghai has drawn up the following provisional measures governing the control of repentant communists:-
(1) These measures are drawn up to govern the supervision of surrendered communists so as to prevent them from relapsing into communist activities and to persuade them to reform.
(2) All communists whose surrender has been approved by this Committee or those communists whose surrender has been approved by an organization of a similar nature as this Committee and who now reside in this city will all come under the supervision of this Committee in accordance with these measures. (Hereafter they will be referred to as surrendered communists.)
(3) Every surrendered communist should, in the first half of each month, submit to this Committee a report on his movements during the previous month. The form of the report will be decided by this Committee.
(4) In case a surrendered communist intends to leave this city, he should submit a petition to this Committee applying for permission to remove so as to enable this Committee to notify the Committee in the district of his destination to supervise his movements on behalf of this Committee.
50797
(5) The guarantor of a surrendered communist should submit to this Committee once every two months a report on the movements of the person he has guaranteed during these two months. The form of the report will be decided by this Committee.
(6) A surrendered communist will be granted exemption of submitting reports if the Committee, after examining the reports above mentioned after a lapse of over one year, holds the view that the surrendered communist will not repeat his former offence. Similar action may be taken if the Committee is requested by the surrendered communist to make an examination of these reports.
(7) In case a guarantor discovers that the person whom he guarantees has committed a repetition of his offence, he should at once report the fact to this Committee or to any proper organization.
(8) A surrendered communist should not fail to put in an appearance under any pretext whenever he is summoned for an interview by this Committee.
(9) In case a surrendered communist fails on two successive occasions to submit a report or to put in an appearance when he is summoned or in case this Committee finds he has committed a repetition of his offence or any other illegal activities, this Committee will have the right to request his arrest.
(10) A repentant communist who, upon his release from a reformatory of the district, comes to reside in this city will be under the supervision of this Committee according to these measures.
(11) These measures have been approved by this Committee for enforcement and have been submitted to the Central Executive Committee for reference.

管制投诚共产党人之措施

为防止悔过共产党人继续从事活动，上海处理共产党人投诚审查委员会制定了以下管制悔过共产党人的暂行措施：-
(1) 制定这些措施是为了管制对投诚共产党人的监督，以防止他们重新从事共产党活动，并劝使他们改过自新。
(2) 所有经本委员会批准投诚的共产党人，或经与本委员会性质相似的组织批准投诚且目前居住在本市的共产党人，均将根据这些措施接受本委员会的监督。（此后将他们称为投诚共产党人。）
(3) 每名投诚共产党人应在每月上半月向本委员会提交一份关于其上个月行踪的报告。报告格式由本委员会决定。
(4) 如果投诚共产党人打算离开本市，他应向本委员会提交申请，请求准许迁移，以便本委员会通知其目的地地区的委员会代表本委员会监督其行踪。
50797
(5) 投诚共产党人的担保人应每两个月向本委员会提交一份关于其所担保人在该两个月内行踪的报告。报告格式由本委员会决定。
(6) 如果本委员会在审查上述报告超过一年后，认为投诚共产党人不会重犯前罪，则可免除其提交报告的义务。如果投诚共产党人请求本委员会审查这些报告，也可采取类似行动。
(7) 如果担保人发现其所担保之人重犯前罪，应立即向本委员会或任何适当机构报告此事。
(8) 投诚共产党人 whenever 被本委员会传唤面谈时，不得以任何借口缺席。
(9) 如果投诚共产党人连续两次未能提交报告或在被传唤时未能出席，或者如果本委员会发现他重犯前罪或从事其他非法活动，本委员会有权要求逮捕他。
(10) 从地区感化院释放后来到本市居住的悔过共产党人，将根据这些措施接受本委员会的监督。
(11) 这些措施已获本委员会批准施行，并已提交中央执行委员会备查。

Sin Wan Pao (Evening Edition) published the following comment
on July 13:-

THE MAD CLAMOUR OF A "GREAT INTIMIDATOR"

Mr. Jones, member of the Labour Party, strongly
condemned the diplomatic policy of the British Government
in the House of Commons. He said: "The British Government
never fails to hold definite views to stimulate weak and
minor countries. But once the clamour of a 'great
intimidator' is heard, the government immediately runs
away." It is a fitting description of Britain's policy
in coping with international problems.
Not only Britain but the whole world has long
ago adopted a policy of cheating the weak and fearing
the strong. Justice and righteousness are forgotten.
Sometimes, a nation, fearing that the insult
to a weak and minor country may prove detrimental to its
own position, comes forward as an arbitrator; but as
soon as a "great intimidator" voices a mad clamour, this
nation will become badly frightened and will not dare
to express any decisive opinion. For this reason, the
world is being dominated by "great intimidators".
Such "great intimidators" are to be found
everywhere, therefore their mad clamour may be heard
at any place. How can the world be peaceful under
such circumstances?
It is unfortunate to be a weak and minor
nation. If a nation does not do its best for itself
but simply asks others for assistance, it will have no
result.

to the nation and the people.

《新闻报》（晚刊）于7月13日发表了以下评论：-

“大恐吓者”的疯狂叫嚣

工党议员琼斯先生在下议院强烈谴责英国政府的外交政策。他说：“英国政府总是不遗余力地持有既定观点来刺激弱小国家。但一旦听到‘大恐吓者’的叫嚣，政府便立即逃跑。”这是对英国应对国际问题政策的恰当描述。
不仅英国，整个世界早已采取了欺弱怕强的政策。正义和公理被遗忘。
有时，一个国家担心侮辱弱小国家可能损害其自身地位，便以仲裁者身份出面；但一旦“大恐吓者”发出疯狂叫嚣，该国便会惊恐万分，不敢表达任何决定性意见。因此，世界正被“大恐吓者”所支配。
这样的“大恐吓者”随处可见，因此他们的疯狂叫嚣在任何地方都能听到。在这种情况下，世界怎能和平？
身为弱小国家是不幸的。如果一个国家不为自己尽力，而只是向他人求助，将不会有结果。

July 15, 1935. Morning Translation.

Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers(July 14):

REGULATIONS GOVERNING THE SURRENDER OF COMMUNISTS

On July 12, the Legislative Yuan at Nanking passed the following regulations governing the surrender of Communists:-
Article 1. Any Communist who surrenders before being discovered may be exempted from punishment, but Communists who have committed any of the crimes mentioned in Article 1 and Article 5 of the Emergency Measures for Offences Against the Security of the Republic of China may have their punishment reduced by 50% or they may be given a suspended sentence. The punishment or a part of the punishment of the above surrendered Communists may be cancelled if they give information of crimes committed by other Communists resulting in the arrest of these Communists or in the seizure of other evidence.
Article 2. If a Communist surrenders when his crimes have been discovered, the punishment for such crimes may be reduced by 50%. The whole or a part of the remaining crimes of such surrendered Communists may be cancelled or the Communists may be given a suspended sentence if they disclose crimes committed by other Communists resulting in the arrest of the latter or in the seizure of other evidence.
Article 3. A Communist wishing to surrender shall do so in writing to the Tangpu with 3 copies of the latest 4-inch half body photograph attached.
Article 4. One representative each from the Provincial Tangpu, the district military and political organs and the Court will be elected to a Committee to Examine Surrendered Communists. In a province where there is a reformatory, a representative of the reformatory will be elected to the Committee.
Article 5. The Committee to Examine Surrendered Communists shall send a surrendered Communist to Court together with the views of the Committee on his case. When a surrendered Communist is exempted from punishment or is given a suspended sentence or the whole of his punishment is cancelled, the Court may permit him to be released on bail or send him to a reformatory. A surrendered Communist whose punishment has been reduced may be sent to a reformatory.
Article 6. A surrendered Communist, after serving more than 50% of his sentence, whose behaviour is fair and where there is evidence to show that he has repented, will be allowed to be released on bail. If the surrendered Communist so bailed out does not commit any crime within the period covered by the remainder of his sentence, he will be considered as having served the whole sentence.
Article 7. As regards the release on bail of surrendered Communists as mentioned in Articles 5 and 6, three reliable guarantors shall prepare a bond to be submitted for approval to the Court of first instance and the Court will then give him a certificate of reform. If surrendered Communists who possess these certificates wish to change their address within two years, they must register such change with the district Tangpu or the police organ. Violation of this Article will be punished with imprisonment.

《新闻报》及其他本地报纸（7月14日）：

共产党人投诚条例

7月12日，南京立法院通过了以下共产党人投诚条例：-
第一条。任何在被发现前投诚的共产党人可免除处罚，但犯有《危害民国紧急治罪法》第一条和第五条所述任何罪行的共产党人，其刑罚可减轻50%或可获缓刑。如果上述投诚共产党人提供其他共产党人犯罪的情报，导致这些共产党人被捕或查获其他证据，其刑罚或部分刑罚可予撤销。
第二条。如果共产党人在其罪行被发现后投诚，此类罪行的刑罚可减轻50%。如果此类投诚共产党人揭发其他共产党人的罪行，导致后者被捕或查获其他证据，其剩余罪行的全部或部分可予撤销，或可对该共产党人判处缓刑。
第三条。希望投诚的共产党人应以书面形式向当地党部投诚，并附上最近拍摄的四寸半身照片三份。
第四条。由省党部、地区军政机关和法院各选出一名代表组成审查投诚共产党人委员会。在设有感化院的省份，感化院的一名代表也将入选该委员会。
第五条。审查投诚共产党人委员会应将投诚共产党人连同委员会对其案件的意见一并送交法院。当投诚共产党人被免除处罚、判处缓刑或其全部刑罚被撤销时，法院可允许其取保释放或将其送往感化院。刑罚减轻的投诚共产党人可被送往感化院。
第六条。服刑超过50%刑期、表现良好且有证据表明其已悔过的投诚共产党人，将被允许取保释放。如果如此取保释放的投诚共产党人在剩余刑期内未犯任何罪行，将被视为已服完全部刑期。
第七条。关于第五条和第六条所述的投诚共产党人取保释放事宜，应由三名可靠的担保人准备保结书，提交初审法院批准，随后法院将向其颁发改过证书。如果持有这些证书的投诚共产党人希望在两年内变更地址，必须向地区党部或警察机关登记此变更。违反本条规定将被处以监禁。

June 6, 1935. Afternoon translation.

A REPENTANT COMMUNIST

The Shanghai Morning Post publishes the
following advertisement:-

"I have been a member of the Chinese
Communist Party for several years during which period
I have held important posts in the organization. Now
I am convinced that the policies of the Communist Party
are unlawful and that its acts are barbarous. The
present general rupture in the party and in the Red Army
under its control proves the failure of Marxism. I
have come to my senses and realize my past mistakes/
I pledge to struggle under the guidance of the Three
Principles of the People so that a national crisis might
be averted. I call upon my former colleagues in the
Communist Party as well as other Communist Party members
to struggle for the nation.

Tsang Wo (張和)"

一名悔悟的共产党员

《上海晨报》刊登如下广告：-

“本人加入中国共产党已有数年，在此期间曾在该组织中担任重要职务。现本人深信，共产党的政策违法，其行为野蛮。目前该党及其控制下的红军内部普遍破裂，证明了马克思主义的失败。本人已幡然醒悟，认识到过去的错误；本人誓在三民主义的指导下奋斗，以挽救民族危机。本人呼吁前共产党同事及其他共产党员为国家而奋斗。

May 13, 1935. Afternoon translation.

COMMITTEE TO EXAMINE CASES OF SURRENDERED COMMUNISTS

The Shanghai Committee to Examine Cases of
Surrendered Communists was inaugurated in November 1934.
Since its inauguration, the Committee has dealt with
more than 100 cases in which Communists asked for permission
to surrender.

In aninterview with our reporter yesterday,
a spokesman of the Committee made the following statement:-
"The Committee has dealt with some 120 cases
of surrendered Communists, amongst which number some 80
have been approved and the Committee has requested the
Woosung-Shanghai Garrison Commiessioner' s Headquarters
to issue each a certificate permitting them to reform.
Some 30 other Communists have been ordered to carry out
the proper procedure for further investigation. The aim
of the Committee is to give a chance to youths seduced
by the Communist Party, to reform. With a view to
preventing persons applying for surrender with false
intention the Committee will not accept a case unless
the Communist concerned can provide a joint guarantee of
three persons having proper business connections in Shanghai.
When a Communist reformer is approved the Committee will
request the Tangpu and other political, military and police
organs to afford him rprotection so as to avoid unnecessary
inconvenience."

1935年5月13日。下午译件。

审查投诚共产党人案件委员会

上海审查投诚共产党人案件委员会于1934年11月成立。自成立以來，该委员会已处理了100多起共产党人请求准许投诚的案件。

该委员会发言人在昨日接受本报记者采访时发表如下声明：“本委员会已处理约120起共产党人投诚案件，其中约80起已获批准，本委员会已请求吴淞上海警备司令总部向每人颁发准许改过自新的证书。另有约30名共产党人被责令履行适当程序以作进一步调查。本委员会的宗旨是给受共产党诱骗的青年一个改过自新的机会。为防止有人怀着虚假意图申请投诚，除非相关共产党人能提供三名在上海有正当业务关系的人的联合担保，否则本委员会不予受理。当一名共产党悔改者获得批准时，本委员会将请求唐浦（音译）及其他政治、军事和警察机关为其提供保护，以避免不必要的麻烦。”

April 25, 1935. Afternoon translation.

A COMMUNIST SECEDES FROM HIS PARTY

The Shanghai Morning Post and other local newspapers
published the following advertisement on April 24:-

In a moment of weakness I was induced
to join the Communists and was made use of by them.
I am now convinced that the activities of the Communist
Party are harmful to China and that the doctrine of the
Three Principles of the People is suitable of application
in China during these dangerous times.

I hereby declare my secession from the
Communist Party and will henceforth observe the Three
Principles of the People.

Tsoong Yoong Shing (鍾榮兴).

April 22, 1935. Morning Translation.

Shanghai Morning Post (official organ of Gen. Chiang Kai Shek)
and other local newspapers:

LARGE NUMBERS OF WENCHOW FISHERMEN COME TO SHANGHAI

On April 12, some 300 fishermen in Wenchow
boarded the s.s. "Foh Ping" (福平) of the Tseng An
Company (振安公司) for Hwa Yao San (花鳥山) and Chen
San (陳山), Tsungming Hsien, to fish as they cannot
find employment at their native place. When the vessel
arrived at the wharf, the fishermen at Tsungming stopped
the Wenchow fishermen from landing and discharged guns
as a demonstration.
Fearing trouble, the Wenchow fishermen returned
to Shanghai by the same vessel on April 20 and landed
at Nantao. They later sent representatives to call at
the Wenchow Fellow Provincials Association to ask for
assistance.
The Wenchow Fellow Provincials Association
ordered the fishermen to remain on the vessel for the
time being. The Bureau of Public Safety and the Water
Police have been requested to accord them protection.
Arrangements are being made to send the fishermen to
their native place.

REFORMED COMMUNISTS

Communists Li Seu Tseng (李秀楨), Lo Sz Hau
(駱士豪), Yu Ai Ling (俞愛林) alias Yu An Ling (俞安玲),
Li Yih Chen (李一誠), Tan Tsa Kan (譚再幹), Zung Ying Ta
(程應達), Chiang Teh Chen (德仁), Chiang Zang Chong
(姜長昌), alias Chiang Chong Chong (姜昌昌), Chen Hai
Ping (成海清), Hau Che (霍徹), Li Chia Tseng (李家震),
Tseu Kwang Yien (周廣言), Chen Ah Hwa (陳阿華), Wong
Doong Ting (王全鼎), Zee Dien Sz (徐田氏), Loo Doong (魯桐)
and Fang Tsoo (方超), all of whom have been sent to the
Kiangsu Reformatory, publish notices in the advertisement
columns of the "Shanghai Morning Post" (Evening Edition)
(official organ of Gen. Chiang Kai Shek) on April 21
denouncing the Chinese Communist Party and declaring that
they will observe the Three Principles of the People and
work for the welfare of the Kuomintang Government.

Shanghai Morning Post (official organ of Gen. Chiang Kai Shek)
and other local newspapers:

YUNG SHING EXCHANGE BANK CLOSES DOWN

The Yung Shing Exchange Bank (永興錢莊),
Shing Chen Li (盛仁里) on Ningpo Road, which was established
four years ago with a capital of $500,000, suspended
business on April 20.
It is learned that the deposits received by
the bank amount to some $1,000,000. Accounts due to the
bank total about the same amount.
Chen Zing Tao (陳靜濤), the manager, has
engaged a lawyer to handle the liquidation.

《上海晨报》（蒋介石将军的官方机关报）及其他本地报纸：

大批温州渔民来沪

4月12日，约300名温州渔民因在家乡无法找到工作，登上振安公司 (Tseng An Company) 的“福平”号 (Foh Ping) 轮船，前往崇明县的花鸟山 (Hwa Yao San) 和陈山 (Chen San) 捕鱼。当船只抵达码头时，崇明渔民阻止温州渔民上岸，并开枪示威。
温州渔民因害怕惹出麻烦，于4月20日乘同一艘船返回上海，并在南市登陆。随后他们派代表拜访温州同乡会寻求援助。
温州同乡会命令渔民暂时留在船上。已请求公共安全局和水警为他们提供保护。正在安排将渔民送回原籍。

改过自新的共产党人

共产党人李秀楨 (Li Seu Tseng)、駱士豪 (Lo Sz Hau)、俞愛林 (Yu Ai Ling) 又名俞安玲 (Yu An Ling)、李一誠 (Li Yih Chen)、譚再幹 (Tan Tsa Kan)、程應達 (Zung Ying Ta)、德仁 (Chiang Teh Chen)、姜長昌 (Chiang Zang Chong) 又名姜昌昌 (Chiang Chong Chong)、成海清 (Chen Hai Ping)、霍徹 (Hau Che)、李家震 (Li Chia Tseng)、周廣言 (Tseu Kwang Yien)、陳阿華 (Chen Ah Hwa)、王全鼎 (Wong Doong Ting)、徐田氏 (Zee Dien Sz)、魯桐 (Loo Doong) 和方超 (Fang Tsoo)，均已被送往江苏感化院，于4月21日在《上海晨报》（晚刊）（蒋介石将军的官方机关报）的广告栏刊登声明，谴责中国共产党，并宣布他们将遵守三民主义，为国民党政府的福祉工作。

《上海晨报》（蒋介石将军的官方机关报）及其他本地报纸：

永興錢莊停业

位于宁波路盛仁里 (Shing Chen Li)、四年前以50万元资本成立的永興錢莊 (Yung Shing Exchange Bank)，于4月20日停止营业。
据悉，该钱庄收到的存款约为100万元。欠该钱庄的账目总额也大致相同。
经理陈静涛 (Chen Zing Tao) 已聘请律师处理清算事宜。

Sin Wen Pao and other local newspapers.

REPENTANT COMMUNIST EXAMINATION COMMITTEE

Since the inauguration by the local Tangpu Head-
quarters, the Woosung-Shanghai Garrison Commissioner's
Headquarters and other local authorities of the Repentant
Communist Examination Committee in November last, many
Communists applied for permission to surrender.

According to information secured yesterday, the
Committee has dealt with the applications of over 50
Communists. There are about 10 Communists who have not yet
completed the necessary formalities in applying for permission
to surrender. Thus their applications will be brought up
for consideration at the next meeting of the Committee.

A COMMUNIST RENOUNCES THE CHINESE COMMUNIST PARTY

Min Pao (official organ of the Kuomintang)
contains the following advertisement published by Yuan Jih
Zu ( 袁 傑 如 ) renouncing his connection with the Chinese

Party."

Political (3)

Shanghai Municipality Surrendered Communist Investigation
Committee - Meeting

D4797
Seven committee members of the above-mentioned committee
held a meeting between 2.30 p.m. and 4 p.m. January 7, 1935,
in the local Kuomintang Headquarters, and passed the follow-
ing resolutions:-

1. That the Woosung-Shanghai Garrison Commander's
Headquarters be informed of the recent application
to surrender by nine communists including one Koo
Wen-ping (顧孟平).

2. That a petition be submitted to the Central Kuomin-
tang for the exemption of criminal punishment of
those surrendered communists who have not committed
violence to endanger the Republic.

3. That the Central Kuomintang be requested to publicly
promulgate measures to deal with surrendered commu-
nists.

4. That the investigation of the application to surren-
der by communists be undertaken by the local Kuomin-
tang Headquarters and the Bureau of Public Safety.

January 8, 1935. Afternoon Translation.

Chen Pao and other local newspapers :

MEETING OF SHANGHAI REFORMED COMMUNIST CASES
EXAMINATION COMMITTEE

At 2 p.m. yesterday the Shanghai Reformed
Communist Cases Examination Committee held a meeting
at the local Tangpu Headquarters, Foong Ling Jao,
Nantao. Representatives from the local Tangpu,
the Shanghai City Government, the Woosung-Shanghai
Garrison Commissioner's Headquarters, the Second and
the Third Branches of the Kiangsu High Court and the
Bureau of Public Safety were present.
The following resolutions were passed :-
1) That Yen Meng Ping (颜孟平) and eight other
communists be permitted to reform and that the
Woosung-Shanghai Garrison Commissioner's Headquarters
be requested to make the necessary arrangements for
the issue to them of reform certificates.
2) That the Central authorities be requested
to revise Article 1 of the Law governing reformed
communists; that those communists who surrender
prior to the issue of reform certificates and who
have not committed any of the offences mentioned in
Articles 1, 2, 5 and 6 of the Offences Against the
Internal Security of the State, shall be exempt from
punishment; and that Article 6 of the Law be
deleted.
3) That the local Tangpu be requested to draft
measures for the control of converted communists.
4) That another meeting be called to discuss
the applications already received from other

昨日，中国引水员协会筹备委员会的一位负责人称，由于除非收回引水权，否则国防将受到损害，该委员会决定向国民政府提交以下几点：

Min Pao and other local newspapers:

SURRENDER OF A FORMER COMMUNIST

(趙用賓), Chao Yeu Nan (趙幼男) alias Chao Yung Ping
), age 24, native of Szechuen, joined the
Communist Party in 1933. He served as a clerk and
as an interpreter attached to the Training Class
of the Party. He was arrested by the Chinese authorities
on July 16, 1934 and has been permitted to surrender.
The surrendered Communist has issued the
following declaration:-
"The situation in China is daily becoming
more critical. What China needs at present is not a
proletarian revolution of the Communist Party, but a
people's revolution under the Three Principles of the People.
Moved by my patriotism, I walked in the wrong path of
Communism during the past year and participated in the
political activities of the Chinese Communist Party.
I have now discovered that the work of the Chinese
Communist Party is impairing the Chinese revolution.
"I have withdrawn from the Chinese Communist
Party and will henceforth work under the guidance of the
Three Principles of the People."

Surrender of Members of the Leftist League.

Moo Moo Tien (穆木天), member of the
Leftist League, was Chief Secretary of the so-called
People's Self Salvation Association to Resist Insult
in 1933.
Waung Han Wen (汪漢雯) joined the minor
sections of the Leftist League in 1932 and was attached
to the Organization Department of the North-East District
Committee in Shanghai in 1933. Later he severed his
connection with the Leftist League owing to disagreement
with fellow members.
Lieu Ts Min (劉智民) joined the Poem &
Song Association in October 1933 and at the end of May
1934 he joined the Leftist League on the introduction
of Yih Lieu (葉流) and Poo Foong (蒲風).
Moo Moo Tien, Waung Han Wen and Lieu Ts Min
have issued a joint declaration severing their connection
with the Leftist League.

Shun Pao and other local newspapers :-

CHINESE DEPORTEES FROM JAPAN LEAVING FOR WENCHOW TODAY

Of the 49 Chinese deported from Japan who are
now in Shanghai, 44 will leave for Wenchow this afternoon
by the s.s. Hai Yien (海晏) of the China Merchants
Steam Navigation Company.
On September 24 the Sin Yuan (新原) Primary
School on Haining Road detailed representatives to
console the deportees and to issue bread and biscuits to
the deportees. They requested the deportees to deliver
an address on their deportation and the ill-treatment
they had received at the hands of the Japanese. The
deportees detailed Zung Vung Ching (陳鳳卿) to deliver
the address.

The Shanghai District Commission For The Investigation Of Surrendered Communists publishes the following notice in the advertisement columns of the Shanghai Pao and other local newspapers:-

THE NEW ZEALAND PERPETUAL FORESTRY COMPANY

Alleging that there are many doubtful points in the subscriptions for shares in Shanghai of the New Zealand Perpetual Forestry Company Ltd., a British concern, the Ministry of Industry has requested the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to make an enquiry about the firm at the British Legation and to give a reply so that the Industry Ministry may take action.

China Evening News dated September 17 :

ATTEMPTED MURDER

At 11.30 p.m. September 16 two desperadoes entered Room No. 34 of the Che Chi Zung Kee (謝吉博記) Hotel, No.37 Shansi Road, and after firing three shots at the occupant of the room, they made good their escape.
The victim is a man named Yung Kuo Hwa (熊國華), age 34, who arrived here from Wenchow about three days ago. He was wounded in three places.
The Louza Police Station at once detailed detectives to conduct an investigation. The victim stated that he had come to Shanghai from Wenchow three days ago for the purpose of visiting relatives here and that he held important positions in the Special Affairs Section and the Propaganda Section of the North-Eastern Volunteer Army. He could not attribute a possible motive for the attempt on his life.
An examination of the bullets which had been extracted from the body of the victim reveals that there is nothing on record regarding these bullets. The Police regard the case as a political affair. A strict investigation is being held.

THE TSAI YANG GEE CASE

The Shanghai First Special District Court has made ten attempts to hear the case in which Long Chu Ying (郎祖蔭), a detective sergeant attached to Louza Station of the Shanghai Municipal Police is charged with having tortured Tsai Yang Gee (蔡洋其) with electricity, but owing to the non-appearance of the detective who ignored the summons issued by the Court against him, the case could not be tried. Judge Liu Yu Kwei (劉毓桂), who is sitting in the case, had issued summonses to the complaint and the accused for their appearance, but when the hearing was opened, the detective again failed to put in an appearance, although Tsai Yang Gee and his wife, the complainants, and Bo Teh Foh (包德福), one of the accused, were present.

September 15, 1934.    Morning Translation.

Chen Pao and other local newspapers:

FIVE SURRENDERED COMMUNISTS

Conditions in China are not suitable for Communism. Numbers of youths have blindly joined the Communist Party but it is not yet too late to repent, for the Central Government has drafted Regulations governing the surrender of Communists and many youths have thus been saved.

Of late five Communists named Wen Jih Zung (文章化), Hu Kwang Hwa (胡光華), Chu Tso Fu (朱作夫), Chen Hung Kwei (陳鴻貴) and Huang Hen (黃痕) alias Zing Kiang (靜江) alias Chen Chen (淺誠) were arrested by the Chinese authorities but have been permitted to surrender.

Wen Jih Zung is a native of Hunan, age 27. He joined the Social Scientists League and the Anti-Imperialist League of the Communist Party after the January 28 Incident. He was an executive member attached to the Propaganda Department of the Anti-Imperialist League as well as member of a Branch of the Social Scientists League. He joined the Communist Party on January 28, 1933 and became a member of the Standing Committee of the Social Scientists League, Chief of the Propaganda Department of the Shanghai Eastern District Committee of the Party, executive member of the Propaganda Department of the Kiangsu Provincial Committee and executive member of the Lenin Livelihood Compiling Committee. At the end of June 1934 he was transferred to the Fah-Nan District as a special member. He was arrested at the beginning of July.

Hu Kwang Hwa, age 28, native of Honan, joined the Communistic Youth League in 1932 and later became a member of the Communist Party. He undertook propaganda work in villages. In December 1933, he was ordered to be transferred to the Honan Provincial Committee to undertake mimeograph work, but the transfer did not materialize owing to his ignorance of mimeograph work. In January 1934, he was transferred to Shanghai to undertake communications work of the Central Committee of the Communist Party.

Chu Tso Fu, male, native of Chekiang, joined the Communist Party in May 1934. He disseminated propaganda in favour of Communism to a Chinese postal worker named Nyi (倪), and was arrested in July 1934.

Chen Hung Kwei, male, age 26, joined the Communistic Youth League in 1926 and later became Chief of the Propaganda Section of the League. He went to Moscow in the following year and studied in the Chung San University. Returning to China in 1929, he severed his connection with the Communist Party. He was arrested on July 23, 1934.

Huang Hen alias Zing Kiang alias Chen Chen, age 27, native of Fukien, joined the Communist Party in 1933. He undertook the printing work of the Party and afterwards became a clerk attached to the Anti-Imperialist League. He arrived in Shanghai at the end of June 1934.

In a joint manifesto, the five surrendered Communists advise youths not to take the wrong course but to work for the extermination of the Communist Party under the flag of the Three Principles of the People.

五名投诚的共产党人

中国目前的局势不适合共产主义。许多青年盲目加入共产党，但现在悔悟为时未晚，因为中央政府已起草了关于共产党人投诚的条例，从而挽救了许多青年。

近期，五名名为文章化（Wen Jih Zung）、胡光華（Hu Kwang Hwa）、朱作夫（Chu Tso Fu）、陳鴻貴（Chen Hung Kwei）和黄痕（Huang Hen）（化名靜江 Zing Kiang，又名淺誠 Chen Chen）的共产党人被中国当局逮捕，但获准投诚。

文章化，湖南人，27岁。一·二八事变后，他加入了共产党的社会科学家联盟和反帝同盟。他是反帝同盟宣传部执行委员，也是社会科学家联盟某分支的成员。他于1933年1月28日加入共产党，并成为社会科学家联盟常务委员会成员、党上海东区委员会宣传部长、江苏省委宣传部执行委员以及列宁生计编纂委员会执行委员。1934年6月底，他被调往法南区（Fah-Nan District）担任特约成员。他在7月初被捕。

胡光華，28岁，河南人，1932年加入共产主义青年团，后成为共产党员。他在农村从事宣传工作。1933年12月，他奉命调往河南省委从事油印工作，但因不懂油印技术，调动未能实现。1934年1月，他被调往上海，从事党中央的联络工作。

朱作夫，男，浙江人，1934年5月加入共产党。他向一名姓倪（Nyi）的中国邮政工人传播支持共产主义的宣传，并于1934年7月被捕。

陳鴻貴，男，26岁，1926年加入共产主义青年团，后成为该团宣传科科长。次年赴莫斯科，在中山大学学习。1929年回国后，他与共产党断绝关系。他于1934年7月23日被捕。

黄痕，化名靜江，又名淺誠，27岁，福建人，1933年加入共产党。他从事党的印刷工作，后成为反帝同盟的一名职员。他于1934年6月底抵达上海。

在这五名投诚的共产党人联合发表的宣言中，他们劝告青年不要误入歧途，而应在三民主义的旗帜下致力于消灭共产党。

September 14, 1934. Morning Translation.

China Times and other local newspapers:

REGULATIONS DEALING WITH REPENTANT COMMUNISTS

The Shanghai District Kuomintang some time ago drew up a set of regulations to deal with repentant communists and submitted them to the Central Government for approval.
At 2 p.m. yesterday, the District Kuomintang, in conjunction with other official organs concerned, inaugurated a Committee for the Investigation of Surrendered Communists and passed the regulations to deal with repentant communists. The Committee is now functioning at the District Kuomintang Headquarters at Fengling Jao, off Route Ghisi.
At a meeting held yesterday under the auspices of the Party Organ, representatives from the Shanghai City Government, the Woosung-Shanghai Garrison Commissioner's Headquarters, the Kiangsu High Court Second Branch, the Kiangsu High Court Third Branch, and the Bureau of Public Safety were present.
After a report had been made by the representatives of the local Kuomintang on the regulations in question, the meeting passed the following resolutions:-
1) That a committee for the investigation of surrendered communists be formed by representatives of the organs present.
2) That the regulations governing the surrendering of communists and the acceptance of such cases by the Shanghai District Kuomintang be promulgated.
3) That a notification be issued informing all communists who had joined the communist party through misunderstanding to register themselves with the committee.
4) That the office of the committee be located at the Shanghai District Kuomintang Headquarters at Fengling Jao, off Route Ghisi.
5) That the committee commence to function at once.

The following are the regulations governing the surrendering of communists and the acceptance of such cases by the Shanghai District Kuomintang as approved by the Central Government:-
Article 1. Communists who surrender themselves before their arrest and who have not violated Articles 1, 2, 5 and 6 relating to the summary punishment of communists for endangering the internal security of the State will be pardoned.
Article 2. The sentences to be passed on communists who have violated Articles 1, 2, 5 and 6 of the Offences Against the Security of the State but who have surrendered, can be reduced by half or be suspended.
Article 3. If the surrendered communists referred to in the previous Article give information which leads to the arrest of other communists or to the seizure of reactionary documents or other evidence, their punishment or a part of their punishment can be remitted.

《字林西报》及其他本地报纸：

处理悔悟共产党人的条例

上海区国民党此前制定了一套处理悔悟共产党人的条例，并提交中央政府批准。
昨日下午2时，区国民党会同其他有关官方机构，成立了投诚共产党人调查委员会，并通过了处理悔悟共产党人的条例。该委员会目前在吉斯路（Route Ghisi）旁枫林桥的上海区国民党总部办公。
在昨日由党组织主持召开的会议上，上海市政府、淞沪警备司令长官公署、江苏高等法院第二分院、江苏高等法院第三分院以及公安局的代表均出席。
在当地国民党代表就有关条例作出报告后，会议通过了以下决议：
1) 由出席机构的代表组成投诚共产党人调查委员会。
2) 颁布关于共产党人投诚及上海区国民党受理此类案件的条例。
3) 发布通知，告知所有因误解而加入共产党的共产党人向委员会登记。
4) 委员会办公室设在吉斯路旁枫林桥的上海区国民党总部。
5) 委员会立即开始运作。

以下是经中央政府批准的、由上海区国民党制定的关于共产党人投诚及受理此类案件的条例：
第一条. 在被捕前主动投诚，且未违反关于危害国家内部安全而对共产党人实施即决惩罚的第1、2、5和6条规定的共产党人，将予以赦免。
第二条. 对于违反了《危害民国紧急治罪法》第1、2、5和6条但已投诚的共产党人，其判刑可减半或缓刑。
第三条. 如果前条所述的投诚共产党人提供线索导致其他共产党人被捕，或查获反动文件及其他证据，可免除其部分或全部刑罚。

REGULATIONS DEALING WITH REPENTANT COMMUNISTS

The Shanghai District Kuomintang some time ago drew up a set of regulations to deal with repentant communists and submitted them to the Central Government for approval.
At 2 p.m. yesterday, the District Kuomintang, in conjunction with other official organs concerned, inaugurated a Committee for the Investigation of Surrendered Communists and passed the regulations to deal with repentant communists. The Committee is now functioning at the District Kuomintang Headquarters at Fengling Jao, off Route Ghisi.
At a meeting held yesterday under the auspices of the Party Organ, representatives from the Shanghai City Government, the Woosung-Shanghai Garrison Commissioner's Headquarters, the Kiangsu High Court Second Branch, the Kiangsu High Court Third Branch, and the Bureau of Public Safety were present.
After a report had been made by the representatives of the local Kuomintang on the regulations in question, the meeting passed the following resolutions:-
1) That a committee for the investigation of surrendered communists be formed by representatives of the organs present.
2) That the regulations governing the surrendering of communists and the acceptance of such cases by the Shanghai District Kuomintang be promulgated.
3) That a notification be issued informing all communists who had joined the communist party through misunderstanding to register themselves with the committee.
4) That the office of the committee be located at the Shanghai District Kuomintang Headquarters at Fengling Jao, off Route Ghisi.
5) That the committee commence to function at once.

The following are the regulations governing the surrendering of communists and the acceptance of such cases by the Shanghai District Kuomintang as approved by the Central Government:-
Article 1. Communists who surrender themselves before their arrest and who have not violated Articles 1, 2, 5 and 6 relating to the summary punishment of communists for endangering the internal security of the State will be pardoned.
Article 2. The sentences to be passed on communists who have violated Articles 1, 2, 5 and 6 of the Offences Against the Security of the State but who have surrendered, can be reduced by half or be suspended.
Article 3. If the surrendered communists referred to in the previous Article give information which leads to the arrest of other communists or to the seizure of reactionary documents or other evidence, their punishment or a part of their punishment can be remitted.

COMMUNISM

The "Shing Pao"(興報), a mosquito paper, published the following report on July 30:-

SECRET MEETING IN EASTERN DISTRICT OF CHINESE COMMUNIST PARTY.

In view of the numerous raids conducted by the local authorities on communist bases, the responsible members of the Chinese Communist Party in the Shanghai Eastern District held a secret meeting the other day at which the following resolutions were passed:-
(1) That commencing from August 1, the 150 communists at present attached to the Eastern District be increased to 450.
(2) That the newly recruited communists be given strict training especially regarding secrecy and technics.
(3) That the labour masses be called upon to participate in the anti-government movement with the expressed motive of opposing the peace pact and the cotton and wheat loan.
(4) That efforts be made to rescue those communists of the Shanghai Eastern District who were recently arrested and that the Mutual Aid Society be requested to afford relief.
(5) That a manifesto be issued to support the World Anti-Imperialist Conference to be held in Shanghai.
(6) That two Distribution Corps, each consisting of ten persons, be formed to disseminate propaganda matters daily among factory workers in the Eastern District, and that the organization of four Picketing Groups, each consisting of twenty persons, and two Slogan Groups, each consisting of ten persons, be accomplished before August 1 so that they can be active when this anniversary approaches.
